problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨3\sqrt{t},\,{csc}^{2}⁡(t)⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨4,\,10⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the components of the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t.$

$v(t)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨3\sqrt{t},{csc}^{2}⁡(t)⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 3{t}^{1/2}\,\text{d}t,\int {csc}^{2}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{3/2}+{C}_{1},-\operatorname{cot}⁡(t)+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(1)=⟨4,10⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨2(1)^{3/2}+{C}_{1},-\operatorname{cot}⁡(1)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨4,10⟩ & =⟨2+{C}_{1},-\operatorname{cot}⁡(1)+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2+{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{1} & =2,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(1)+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{2} & =10+\operatorname{cot}⁡(1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
v(t)=⟨2t\sqrt{t}+2,\,-\operatorname{cot}⁡(t)+10+\operatorname{cot}⁡(1)⟩.
$$
